name: Trap-Bar Deadlift
movementPattern: Hip hinge and knee extension - vertical pull
grip: Neutral grip holding the dual parallel side handles of the trap bar.
description: Stand centered inside a hexagonal trap bar, hinge at the hips and bend knees to grip the neutral side handles, and drive through the floor to stand fully erect.
setup: Stand centered inside the trap bar with feet hip- to shoulder-width apart.
Hinge at the hips and bend knees until hands can grip the neutral side handles firmly.
Keep chest lifted, shoulders pulled back and down, and spine neutral.
instructions: Push forcefully through the floor with feet to drive hips and knees into extension simultaneously.
Keep arms straight and handles centered along the mid-thigh as you stand tall.
Lock out hips and knees with a tall posture without leaning backward.
Reverse the movement by hinging hips back and bending knees to return weights to the floor under control.
commonMistakes: Hyperextending the lower back at the top lockout.
Allowing the knees to cave inward during the drive.
Jerking the bar off the floor rather than building tension.

logging.example: Trap bar (25 kg) plus 75 kg plates: record 100 kg total mass.
logging.note: Record total combined mass including the trap bar frame and all loaded weight plates.

variantNote: Neutral-grip trap bar variation. Positions the load in line with the body's center of mass, reducing lumbar shear forces relative to a conventional straight barbell.
reviewNotes: Depicts low/standard handle orientation with neutral grip centered inside hexagonal frame.
